matching: Rules are evaluated in order. The first matching rule owns the heading. The final catch-all applies only to the pinned source revision.

statuses.native: Soulfire exposes the concept directly through its protocol and official SDKs.
statuses.different-semantics: Soulfire exposes the concept through a remote, server-authoritative model instead of Mineflayer's in-process object model.
statuses.sdk-convenience: The official SDK composes the behavior from native streams and actions.
statuses.server-task: Soulfire runs the operation as a durable server-side task near the game loop.
statuses.plugin-extension: A permissioned Soulfire plugin owns the feature and publishes it through plugin RPC, task, event, or service descriptors.
statuses.raw-protocol: The stable semantic API does not model this packet-level operation; advanced callers can use the versioned raw protocol API.
statuses.intentionally-unsupported: Soulfire deliberately does not reproduce this in-process extension mechanism.
